properties.name: dec:advisory-concurrency (accepted 2026-07-25, "never by exclusion") rests on a model that was retired on 2026-09-27. It publishes claims by git push, settles crossings by git order, and rejects a lock partly because a lock "contradicts dec:multi-writer-architecture", which is now superseded. Its other reason, the 2026-07-25 outage, reads as the store's one-writer-per-process lock, not a lock on a region
properties.statement:
Read 2026-09-29, while answering Anthony's "islands" brainstorm (dec:idea-a-claimed-blast-radius-is-an-island-no-other-session-writes-in). All of it comes from reading the nodes. No code was read.

1. WHAT THE ACCEPTED DECISION SAYS. dec:advisory-concurrency: "publish it by pushing it... the winner is whichever landed first in git history". It rejects "a coordination service or lock manager" for two reasons: "(contradicts dec:multi-writer-architecture, and single-writer exclusion is the observed failure)". Its rationale adds: "a lock is exactly what took five of six sessions offline on 2026-07-25".

2. THE FIRST REASON IS GONE. dec:multi-writer-architecture ("Many writers keep the repo file and merge on pull — no hosted service") is superseded, and get_node reads it discontinued. Anthony, 2026-09-27, in dec:idea-one-blueprint-the-store-is-the-design-and-an-export-is-a-perishable-photocopy: "Let's reverse the 07-25 rule - let's retire sharing design through git". Under the settled rules, a design IS its server's store and people share it by sharing that server. The git push that published a claim and the git order that settled a crossing are therefore no longer how writers meet. Every writer now reaches the design through one server, which could see every claim at the moment of a write. The advisory design ruled that out, because it had no server.

3. THE SECOND REASON IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF LOCK. The 2026-07-25 outage reads as the store's own exclusion: one writer per process, so a second server could not open the graph. req:sessions-share-a-graph was written the next day ("The store is single-writer per process... there is still exactly one writer"). That lock covered the whole design and could not be released, which is a different thing from a lock on one claimed region that expires. NOT VERIFIED: that the outage was that lock and nothing else. This is inferred from the two records' dates and wording.

4. WHAT STILL STANDS, and it is not weaker. Measured, claim liveness is wrong in both directions:
- fact:two-active-sessions-claims-both-read-gone-2026-09-22: both active sessions' claims read `gone`.
- fact:root-cause-an-idle-session-expires-and-the-proxy-silently-takes-a-new-seat-so-live-claims-read-gone: an idle session silently takes a new seat.
Any enforcement built on today's liveness would either strand a region or lock an agent out of its own region.

⇒ The decision is still accepted and nothing here changes it. Reopening it is Anthony's call. This records only that the question it answered was asked in a world that has since changed.
